analysis.title: GS Basics - Jensen Back. Commodities/China. Bear Mkt for Inflation.
key_insights: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO before the US open Monday and NVDA is +31.5% in a massive squeeze after shorts were added into the end of last week. Author says the return removes some doubt about Nvidia's willingness to keep underwriting the AI buildout.
The AI rally spread across supply chain and Asia: CoreWeave +22%, Taiwan +9% with TSMC and Foxconn limit up, Kospi +6.5% led by Samsung and SK Hynix, Nikkei +4%.

China barely participated: CSI 300 +0.14% and Hang Seng -0.73% in early trade. Watch whether Commerce grants licenses for Chinese customers to access advanced chips via offshore data centers, and whether Congress builds veto-proof support for tougher chip restrictions. Jensen testifies Dec. 1.
Chinese 10yr yield at 1.586%, at or near lows for the year, 5 years and decade, read as structurally unencouraging for China growth and disinflation.

Rates: the back end barely moved with Nasdaq up 6.5%. The front end gave back some of Friday's rally and the curve flattened. 2y inflation swaps appear to have slipped through the bottom of their range.

Energy: Brent is below $90, differentials are offered and US refining cracks are well off highs. Dubai Dec-Jan backwardation fell from $3.67/bbl in October to $0.16/bbl, and the prompt spread is near contango. Author thinks Iran's grip on the marginal barrel is weakening and the market is moving toward balance or surplus.

Fed: Williams was more balanced than Waller or Logan and left successive hikes on the table if data warrant. He sees inflation going from about 3.5% this year to just above 2% next year. December is effectively priced, and falling commodities plus AI spend questions could shift the market to trade the last hike of the cycle.

Risk: author calls price action bear market style, too violent to hold. Best outcome is a couple of quiet days so excess vol premium bleeds and systematics can re-lever, with year-end seasonals as support. Shorts are underwater and are unlikely to have flipped long.
Watch list: IFO, Dell, Workday, 5yr auction, consumer confidence (first print after the sell-off), dollar and commodities.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's return as CEO lifted shares 31.5% in a short squeeze and reduces doubt on Nvidia underwriting the AI buildout.
CoreWeave +22% as the Nvidia CEO news mattered for AI buildout financing.

earnings_insights: Dell and Workday earnings are on the watch list for the coming session. No estimates are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: At or near lows for the year, 5 years and decade, a weak signal for China growth and disinflation.
Oil slipping as more barrels leave the Gulf, supportive for inflation and rates.
Prompt tightness nearly gone, market near balance or surplus.

macro_indicators.reading: about 3.5% this year to just above 2% next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Projected disinflation supports the case for the last hike of the cycle.

risk_factors: Another serious escalation involving Iran could reverse the oil decline.
Violent bear-market-style price action in equities.
Tougher US chip restrictions backed by Congress.
Shorts not yet flipped long, so further squeeze or renewed selling are both possible.
vol_and_positioning: Shorts added into end of last week and are now deeply underwater, fueling a massive squeeze in NVDA.
Excess vol premium needs to bleed out and systematics need room to re-lever, which could create demand with year-end seasonals.
Credit did not have the same beta as equities on the day.
Nasdaq +6.5% with little back-end rates move.
geopolitical: Iran's hold on the marginal barrel from the Gulf appears to be weakening, barring another serious escalation.
US administration tightened rules on remote access to advanced chips for Chinese customers last week, and Congress may push for tougher chip restrictions.
Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify Dec. 1.
